props.text: Live readings, material status and the honest limits.
A figure appears only when the matching scope is granted and the device can read it; otherwise GameCore draws an em dash.

The live control is the host's Glass Control Center, backed by the plugin setting glass_intensity. This bar is a static readout.
Android 12 and newer can blur the backdrop. Below Android 12 the same translucency, gloss and rim render against a sharp backdrop.

Everything else in this suite is a read-only design reference. No screen node dispatches an action, and no plugin code runs.
Everyday look, all five widgets visible
Command card and live vitals in reach
Profile names are a design study, not switches. GameCore's own profiles are the only ones this plugin can change, and it does not change them.
Theme language, palette and shape — previewed, not switched.
The active package carries one theme: OLED Nebula. The other cards show where a sibling theme package could take the same layout language.
The format carries one global radius and one bundled font family. A theme can lean those; it cannot ship a font file or set a per-card radius.
These cards are comparisons, not controls. GameCore's plugin screens attach no gesture, so a tap changes nothing here.
One slow sheen, one soft landing, no fake toggles.
The host reads these values and decides what the device can render. A user who turns animations off gets no sheen and no settle.
A panel should arrive and stop. The gentle spring is a landing, not a performance.
A single sheen drift makes the surface read as material; faster reads as a broken gradient.
System animation settings win over the theme. Motion is never a prerequisite for reading the screen.
The plugin format exposes no animation toggle to a theme. The sheen and spring above are the authored contract; the host owns the frames and the accessibility override.
Three dock studies and the tokens the host really applies.
Tighter icons for a smaller footprint
The dock inherits the same translucent, rimmed material as every panel. There is no separate dock-glass toggle in this package.
1.0× UI scale; your density setting is untouched
The dock cards are layout studies, not dock controls. A data-only plugin cannot resize the host dock or move its icons.
A ramp, a swatch book and the pairs that carry the look.
Body text — rounded, medium, comfortably spaced.
Every enforced text/fill pair in the theme clears WCAG AA; the two body pairs clear AAA. The host computes the final Material roles.
The format lets a theme name a bundled face, not ship one. This package names the rounded family and leaves the device's accessibility scale alone.
A design language for tuning — not a tuning control.
Balances the host's own profile with the current game.
A calmer surface for long sessions and warm devices.
The suite's reference: full glass, live vitals, no drama.
The most vivid look, for short sessions on cool hardware.
These cards are a visual study. GameCore's performance engine, your profiles and the device's thermal state decide what actually runs.
What this plugin does not do
It does not change refresh rate or resolution.
It does not alter CPU, GPU or thermal policy.
It does not run automations or execute code.
It does not hide the host's own performance controls.
What is live, what is a preview, and what the format cannot do.
This package carries JSON and a launcher-icon request. It has no classes, scripts, network calls, WebView or arbitrary host behaviour.
GameCore interprets the theme, screens, settings and widgets with its own native renderer. A malformed package can fail to load; it cannot run.

The design language is inspired by modern storefront interface patterns: true-black surfaces, large rounded cards, lavender/pink accents, glass materials and calm motion. No third-party artwork, screenshots, names or trademarks are included, and this package is not affiliated with any storefront app.
